I now have enough evidence to finalize. Key verification results this pass:

1. **`updateCalendarAttendees`**: grep of `packages/core` returns no matches — confirms the existing finding that the handler calls a non-existent EventManager method (TypeError on every invocation, after the DB write).
2. **`userPrimaryEmail`**: exists in `schema.prisma` (line 558, within the model block following `model Attendee` at 526) — the field exists in the schema, so `booking?.userPrimaryEmail` is not a missing-field bug. Dismissed.
3. **i18n keys `new_guests_added`/`guests_added_event_type_subject`**: found only in the new templates — but the *existing, working* key `your_event_has_been_scheduled` also returns no locale-JSON match in the grep index, so I cannot distinguish "missing key" from "locale files not indexed". Not verifiable → not reported (speculative per instructions).
4. **`@@unique([bookingId, ...])`**: no match in any `.prisma` file — the Attendee table has no DB-level uniqueness guard on `(bookingId, email)`.
5. **Concrete missed bug**: the filter at lines 74-78 only removes guests already present in `booking.attendees` or blacklisted — it never deduplicates **within the input array**. The schema (`z.array(z.string().email())`) allows duplicates like `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]`, so `uniqueGuests` keeps both, and `createMany` (lines 100-104) inserts two identical attendee rows (no unique constraint to stop it), producing duplicate calendar attendee entries and duplicate invite emails. The same check-then-act gap with no transaction/unique constraint also permits duplicates under concurrent requests. This is distinct from all 7 existing findings (which cover the `&&` logic error, missing method, raw-`guests` email fanout, wrong credentials, blacklist case mismatch, unbounded array, and `findFirstOrThrow`).

Lens summary: **bug** — the in-array dedup defect (reported); case-sensitive attendee comparison on line 76 dismissed as a variant of the existing case-normalization finding (same filter expression, same root cause); `disableGuests`/seats bypass dismissed as intentional organizer action. **security** — authorization gate flaws already covered (the `&&` bug restricts rather than broadens; no new bypass beyond the covered blacklist case). **performance** — unbounded array already covered; per-attendee `getTranslation` Promise.all is bounded by booking size, not material; no new findings.
